title: Eq 9.1 leaves R and P undefined against the bucket list: on the Ch30 example its four readings give $104.10, $200, $4.10 or $100, and only the last is correct

locations.quote: Separately track policy buckets: unallocated capital, session allocations, protected proceeds, order reservations and operational buffers. Policy buckets are claims on economic assets, not additional assets.
already committed cash $R$, protected proceeds $P$ and operational buffer $B$
These terms must be disjoint.
The session retains $9.90 cash plus $95.90 receivable, totaling $105.80. Completion protects both components.
if session["cash"] < cls.reserved(state, sid):

explanation: Ch9 line 7 lists order reservations as a policy bucket next to session allocations. The reference nests them instead: engine.py:129 asserts that session cash covers the session's reservations. Read as peers, summing the buckets counts reserved cash twice. Eq 9.1 has the same problem. R is 'already committed cash' and the book never says whether session allocations count as committed. P is 'protected proceeds', and per Ch30 that includes a $95.90 unsettled receivable that is not part of min(C_b,C_l). Re-derived on Ch30, with H=B=0 and C_b=C_l=$209.90 once the buy has settled. The true free settled cash is $200 at A's completion and $100 after B is funded with $100. At completion, the readings that subtract all of P give 209.90-105.80 = $104.10 (understated by $95.90); the settled-P readings give $200 (correct). After B is funded: (a) R = reservations only, P in full: $104.10, over by $4.10. (b) R = reservations only, P settled part: $200, over by $100. Because 9.1 does not fall when an allocation is made, allocations keep passing again and again. (c) R includes allocations, P in full: $4.10, under by $95.90, which blocks a legitimate allocation. (d) R includes allocations, P settled part: $100, correct. Only one of the four readings is right, and two of them are not conservative.
proposed_resolution: Keep two books. (1) The economic journal holds cash, receivables, payables, accrued fees and inventory at cost. (2) The policy owner dimension holds Unallocated U, Session S_s, Protected P_s, ExternalOwner X, OperationalBuffer B and ReviewHold. Order reservations are holds inside S_s and never a peer bucket. Invariant per (account, currency): the sum over all owners of their economic balances equals the account's economic balance. Rewrite 9.1 as F = min(C_b, C_l) - H - B - sum over non-Unallocated owners of only the settled-cash component of each owner's claim. Equivalently, F = the settled cash owned by Unallocated, capped by broker settled cash net of holds. Seed allocation: seed <= F, using atomic compare-and-reserve. Buy order: p*q*M + fee_envelope <= S_s settled cash - open holds of S_s, and also <= F. Add a test that replays Ch30 and asserts F = $200 at A's completion and F = $100 after B is funded.
verifier_note: Quotes and arithmetic re-checked. The original claimed that 'a second $100 allocation' would be wrongly approved. That was imprecise: under reading (a), F=$104.10 against a true $100, so a second $100 is actually fundable and the over-approval is $4.10. Under reading (b) the over-approval is unbounded, because repeated allocations all pass. Also, ADR-0006 (docs/adr) restates 9.1 as 'minus every non-outside claim'. That still needs the settled-cash-component restriction, or it reproduces readings (a) and (c).

disposition.resolution: Funding is bounded per owner, not by a residual formula. A seed moves only out of `unallocated`'s available cash (CASH + PAYABLE + FEES_ACCRUED minus active cash holds and net payments due on sales) less the operational buffer. Receivables are never available, protected proceeds are a separate owner, and ledger CASH is confirmed only when it equals broker settled cash. This is reading (d) of the finding: free cash = settled cash owned by unallocated.

title: Residual equity of stopped, below-target or risk-stopped sessions has no destination bucket, and the reference deadlocks permanently after RISK_STOP

locations.quote: A session can terminate unsuccessfully, wait indefinitely for an admissible opportunity or be stopped by the owner.
The proposed default is to stop and require the ordinary session evaluation path, rather than oscillating automatically between liquidation and re-entry.
`COMPLETED_UNSETTLED`, `COMPLETED_SETTLED`, `STOPPED` and `FAILED_REVIEW`
if session["state"] != "RUNNING" or session["positions"] or p.get("fees_final") is not True:
if any(x["state"] == "RISK_STOP" for x in state["sessions"].values()):

explanation: The book says what happens to a successful session's equity (it is protected). It never says where the cash and receivables of a STOPPED or FAILED_REVIEW session go, or of a session that wound down below target, and it never defines the transitions into those states. Engineers will diverge. One will return the residual, receivables included, to Unallocated at once; if availability does not exclude receivables, that breaks 'no funding from receivables'. Another will leave it in the dead session's bucket forever, so authorized capital leaks away. In the reference, a RISK_STOP session can never complete, because complete requires RUNNING (engine.py:293), so its cash is stranded. A probe on a temporary copy confirmed this. After RISK_STOP and a process restart, 'start' is rejected ('risk-stopped session requires review'), a risk-reducing SELL is rejected ('unreconciled or inactive session') because reconciled is only set by start, and a new session is rejected. No command leads out of that state. RISK_STOP is also not one of the book's ten states.
proposed_resolution: Terminal accounting for unsuccessful sessions. (1) Termination needs the same evidence as completion: flat inventory, no open or UNKNOWN orders, final fees and a clean reconciliation. (2) STOPPED (owner end, or wound down below target): the residual is re-owned to Unallocated. Receivables keep their availability class, so only confirmed settlement makes them spendable. (3) FAILED_REVIEW (risk trigger, exception, the reference's RISK_STOP): the residual moves to ReviewHold and is released to Unallocated only by an authenticated owner command. (4) Unsuccessful sessions never get a successor. (5) Losses stay in the aggregate loss counters. (6) A risk-stopped account must still accept owner-authorized risk-reducing sells after reconciliation, without clearing the stop latch. Map the reference's RISK_STOP to FAILED_REVIEW.
verifier_note: Confirmed in the book and by running a probe on a temporary copy of reference/engine.py. ADR-0008 already chooses to split STOPPED into SUSPENDED and CLOSED, and has CLOSED re-own the residual and its receivables to unallocated. That is consistent with this resolution provided receivables stay non-available.

disposition.resolution: ADR-0008: an unsuccessful session (BELOW_TARGET, OWNER_ENDED, EXPIRED) ends CLOSED once flat, fee-final and reconciled. Its cash returns to `unallocated` and its receivables are re-owned to `unallocated` but stay non-available until settlement confirms them; no successor is created. A session risk trigger suspends the session (reductions still allowed) and the owner can end it, so nothing deadlocks.
disposition.residual: No ReviewHold owner: FAILED_REVIEW keeps the session's balances in session:<id> until the owner resolves the case (see BR-SES-05).

title: No rule for fee adjustments, corrections or busts that arrive after completion and protection, and 'sufficiently finalized' fees is undefined

locations.quote: If the broker later changes a fee, record an adjustment linked to the original execution and update performance without rewriting history. Retain a fee buffer before making funds reusable.
Completion requires flat inventory, no unresolved orders, reconciled net proceeds and sufficiently finalized fees.
Execution busts and corrections require reversal entries plus replacement events.
if session["state"] == "COMPLETED" and (session["positions"] or session["cash"]):

explanation: 'Sufficiently finalized' is never defined. Changes that arrive after completion can do three things. (a) A fee change or price correction can push terminal equity below the goal after the successor request was created on the strength of that success. (b) A bust can reverse a protected receivable that will then never settle. (c) A bust can restore inventory to a COMPLETED session. The book does not say which bucket absorbs the change, whether 'success' is revoked, or what happens to a funded successor. The reference has no fee-adjustment, correction or bust command, and fees_final is a caller assertion. Its invariant at engine.py:136 forbids a COMPLETED session from holding inventory or cash, so a direct port of that invariant would make case (c) raise and roll back.
proposed_resolution: (1) Completion requires a final fee record for every execution of the session. For IBKR that means a commissionReport for every execId; an estimate-only fee blocks completion. (2) A later adjustment posts to the completed session's Protected bucket, linked to the original execution. (3) If corrected terminal equity falls below the goal, the session is flagged COMPLETED_RESTATED for owner review. The successor is not unwound: it was funded from independent unallocated cash, so no money was duplicated. (4) A bust that restores inventory moves that inventory and its cost into ReviewHold, not the completed session, freezes new entries and opens an exception. (5) If Protected would go negative, record the shortfall as an exception claim and halt. Never take it silently from Unallocated or from session buckets.
verifier_note: Quotes verified. The original said the reference 'would throw an AssertionError on (c)'. There is no reference command that can restore inventory, so that is true only of a direct port of the invariant at line 136; the wording has been tightened. Ch9 line 29 disclaims the simulator, but the book still gives no production rule. ADR-0008 decides 'late fees and corrections after completion post against protected:<id>; the completion stands'.

disposition.resolution: 'Fees final' is defined: completion needs a broker commission or an owner-accepted estimate for every session execution. Whatever arrives after a session ended is booked to whoever holds its balances now (protected:<id> after completion, unallocated after close; ADR-0008 amendment), and the completion and successor stand. A late fee posts there with a case (blocking if that owner's cash would go negative). A late fill, a bust (a correction to quantity zero, which used to fail the whole command and discard the broker fact) or a price correction is booked there and opens one blocking POST_COMPLETION_ADJUSTMENT per execution; a bust of a buy whose shares were already sold restates the sale's cost there; a cash shortfall moves to exception:<case>. Inventory left in protected:<id> or unallocated is sold by an owner DISPOSAL intent that reserves and books only that owner's lots, runs the full pretrade (the owner's disposal stands in for the session-state check, as the decision records) and reconciles like any trade; a bust, correction or fee change of a disposal fill opens a case too.
disposition.residual: The reviewer's COMPLETED_RESTATED flag was not adopted: a completion is never restated (ADR-0008), and the owner reviews the case instead. Neither the terminal nor the CLI offers a DISPOSAL form; the owner sends submit_intent with purpose DISPOSAL through POST /api/commands (RB-14).

title: The successor's seed, goal and policy snapshot appear only in examples, and 'limited seed recycle' has no amount or timing

locations.quote: A successful transition has a single successor request keyed by the completed session identifier.
A session snapshots it at creation; ordinary owner changes apply to future sessions.
funding eventually runs out unless the owner permits a limited seed recycle or adds authorized capital
"automatic_seed_recycling": false,
state["requests"][request_id] = {"state": "WAITING_FUNDS", "seed": session["seed"], "goal": session["goal"]}

explanation: No rule states the successor's seed and goal. They could be the parent's seed, the current policy default, or the parent's terminal equity (compounding, $105.80 in Ch30). Only the examples (B receives $100) and the reference (parent seed and goal) suggest an answer. It is also unclear whether a successor that waits in WAITING_FUNDS snapshots the policy at request time or at funding time, which may be weeks later after policy edits. 'Limited seed recycle' and automatic_seed_recycling have no amount (the seed? min(seed, settled protected)?), no timing (on completion or on settlement) and no frequency limit. The result is different allocation sizes, and possibly money taken from Protected.
proposed_resolution: The successor request records an immutable mandate: seed = parent seed, goal = parent goal, same currency, plus the policy hash current when the request was created. At funding, re-validate against the current policy. Emergency restrictions always apply. Any other policy difference keeps the request in WAITING_FUNDS with the blocker 'policy changed: owner re-approval required'. Seed recycling, only when automatic_seed_recycling=true, moves exactly min(parent seed, settled protected value) from Protected to Unallocated after COMPLETED_SETTLED, at most once per parent. The profit always stays protected.
verifier_note: Narrowed. The original also claimed that R06's word 'rollover' contradicts protection. Refuted: R06's evidence is 'Conservation and one-successor tests' (Ch30 line 46) and Ch10 defines the mechanism, so 'rollover' means successor creation. The '$105.80 taken from protected funds' reading is excluded by Ch10 line 25. Severity lowered to medium: every reading still funds from Unallocated.

disposition.resolution: ADR-0007: a successor's mandate (seed, target, currency, eligibility, risk terms, policy_hash) is snapshotted from the default active when the successor request is created and frozen; later defaults never change it, and only an owner amendment of an unfunded request issues a new audited version. Seed recycling is not offered: policy schema 1 refuses reinvest_protected_proceeds.

title: The execution table has no provider revision or group key, so a related-identifier correction is stored as a second independent fill (double count) unless an unspecified rule sets correction_of

locations.quote: provider_execution_id TEXT NOT NULL, correction_of TEXT REFERENCES execution(execution_id),
UNIQUE(provider, account_key, provider_execution_id)
Event identifiers alone are insufficient when a provider sends amended content under a related identifier. Keep provider version/correction fields
Each broker execution is deduplicated by its documented stable key, including account scope.

explanation: Ch9 requires provider version/correction fields and warns that identifiers alone are not enough. The schema has correction_of but no revision column and no group key. It also says nothing about how correction_of gets set. IBKR's API documents that a corrected execution arrives as an additional execDetails with every field identical except the execId, which differs only after its final period. Under UNIQUE(provider, account_key, provider_execution_id) that correction is a new, valid row. If nothing links it to the original, quantity and cash are booked twice. Conversely, a provider that re-sends amended content under the same id cannot be stored at all.
proposed_resolution: Execution key = (provider, account_key, provider_execution_id), plus provider_revision and execution_group_id, both derived by documented per-provider rules (IBKR: group = execId without its final revision segment; revision = that segment). Canonicalize the economic fields: qty, price, scales, side, currency, fees, trade and settlement dates. Same key with identical canonical content is a duplicate and a no-op. A new revision in an existing group inserts a row, then posts one journal transaction that reverses the prior revision's lines and books the replacement; it also opens an exception and freezes new exposure for the owner. Ingestion never rejects or drops a broker execution. Add a test in which an IBKR-style .01 to .02 correction leaves the position at the corrected quantity, not double.
verifier_note: Reframed. The original's 'contradiction ... genuine corrections are discarded' rested on engine.py:217. Ch9 line 29 and Ch31 line 13 explicitly disclaim that as simulator-only behaviour. The real defect is the missing revision and group key, which makes a related-id correction look like a new fill (over-count). Kind changed to omission.

disposition.resolution: Executions are keyed by a provider-scoped exec_key. A correction carries correction_of (the IBKR adapter derives it from the execId revision suffix and links to the latest prior revision) and is booked as reversing entries plus a replacement, never as a second fill. A re-delivery with identical economics is a no-op.
disposition.residual: Same execution id with changed content is tracked in BR-ORD-05.

title: Ch9 says the appendix schema specifies lots and fees, but it has no lot, fee, reservation, settlement-obligation, policy-bucket or successor-request tables

locations.quote: The production schema in the appendix specifies journal entries, lots and fees. Its implementation remains a required gate
<!-- INCLUDE: contracts/ledger_schema.sql -->
-- Cross-posting balance, policy authorization, and outbox recovery require service logic.
After approval, commit reservation and durable outbox in one transaction.
Maintain estimated and final amounts separately.

explanation: The appendix schema (Appendix B includes contracts/ledger_schema.sql) has only these tables: policy_version, instrument, session, order_intent, execution, journal_transaction, journal_posting and outbox. It has no lot or lot-disposal table and no fee table with separate estimated and final amounts. It has no reservation table, although Ch13 requires the reservation and the outbox row to commit in one transaction. It also has no settlement-obligation table and nothing for policy buckets or successor requests. Implementers will invent incompatible shapes, or keep reservations only in memory, where a restart loses them.
proposed_resolution: Add these tables to the foundation schema. reservation(reservation_id, command_id, session_id, account_key, currency, cash_units, cash_scale, fee_envelope_units, qty_units, qty_scale, state, released_by_event_id). fee(execution_id, component, currency, estimated_units, final_units, scale, status, source_event_id). lot(lot_id, account_key, instrument_id, owner, acquired_execution_id, trade_date, qty_units, qty_scale, cost_units, fee_units, cost_scale, currency) and lot_disposal(lot_id, disposal_execution_id, qty, relieved_cost). settlement_obligation(obligation_id, source_transaction_id, direction, account_key, currency, amount_units, scale, expected_date, calendar_version, state). policy_movement(movement_id, from_owner, to_owner, currency, amount_units, scale, command_id). successor_request(parent_session_id UNIQUE, mandate_json, policy_hash, state). Write the reservation and the outbox row in the same SQL transaction.
verifier_note: Confirmed by listing every CREATE TABLE in contracts/ledger_schema.sql. Ch31 line 13 also concedes that 'the average-cost pool is not tax-lot accounting'.

disposition.resolution: The core schema (not contracts/ledger_schema.sql) has lots, holds (reservations), settlements (obligations with expected date, relieved account code and owner), postings with an owner column (the policy buckets), successors (UNIQUE predecessor) and executions carrying fee_estimate and fee_final. Holds, the order and its outbox row commit in one event.

title: Money and price columns have no scale or currency, and the scale sits on a single mutable instrument row

locations.quote: Every amount has a currency and scale.
currency TEXT NOT NULL, seed_units INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(seed_units > 0),
limit_price_units INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(limit_price_units > 0),
price_scale INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(price_scale >= 0),
A changed price scale is not a harmless field rename.
| Effective interval | UTC timestamps | Non-overlapping versions |

explanation: session.seed_units and goal_units have no scale. order_intent stores quantity_units and limit_price_units with no scale, no currency and no instrument metadata version, even though the OrderIntent dataclass (broker_port.py lines 21 and 23) carries quantity_scale and price_scale. The scale can therefore only be read from instrument.price_scale. That row is keyed by instrument_id alone (one row, not versioned), contrary to Ch3's non-overlapping versions. If the row changes, every historical order's limit is silently re-scaled. For example, 900 units means $9.00 at scale 2 but $0.09 at scale 4; sub-dollar US stocks may be quoted in $0.0001 increments.
proposed_resolution: Every money or quantity column carries its own scale column, and money carries its currency on the row: seed_units/seed_scale, goal_units/goal_scale, and on order_intent: currency, price_scale, quantity_scale and instrument_metadata_version. Version instrument metadata in instrument_version(instrument_id, version, effective_from, effective_to, price_scale, quantity_scale, multiplier_num, multiplier_den), with non-overlapping intervals. Choose a storage price scale at least as fine as any tick the instrument can ever have (US equities: 4) and never reduce it. Validate tick size and quantity increment separately from storage scale.
verifier_note: Columns checked line by line. The arithmetic (900 units at scale 2 = $9.00, at scale 4 = $0.09) is correct.

disposition.resolution: Every amount and price is stored as canonical decimal text that carries its own scale (ADR-0004), postings and orders carry their currency, and a journal amount must be exact at its currency's ledger scale. A change to instrument metadata cannot re-scale a stored order or posting.
disposition.residual: Instrument metadata is one current row (a change needs a higher metadata_version); earlier versions survive only in the InstrumentRegistered events, and the version rule has no test.

title: Buys have no unsettled payable, so ledger 'settled cash' falls on trade date and cannot be reconciled exactly against broker settled cash

locations.quote: Track settled cash, unsettled receivables, fee liabilities, position inventory and external capital flows.
A purchase transfers value from cash to inventory plus expense.
Buying ten shares at $9 with a $0.10 fee produces $90 inventory, $209.90 total cash and $0.10 expense.
compare open orders, positions, cash and fees; classify differences
Never use a broad monetary tolerance to hide one missing order.

explanation: Sales create an unsettled receivable, but purchases reduce cash on trade date; no unsettled payable exists in Ch9's account list or in the reference (engine.py:233). The ledger's cash is then neither trade-date cash nor settlement-date cash. Between trade date and T+1 after a $90.10 buy, the broker's settlement-date cash still shows $300 while the ledger shows $209.90. Every buy day, reconciliation will either report a cash break and block entries, or someone will add the broad tolerance that line 49 forbids. Buy settlement and failed buy settlement are never modelled; the expected/pending/confirmed/exception machine is described only for proceeds.
proposed_resolution: Add an unsettled-payable account. A buy posts on trade date: Dr inventory (p*q*M), Dr fee expense, Cr payable. Buy settlement posts Dr payable, Cr settled cash. Availability subtracts payables at once, so settled cash - payables - holds gives the same conservative $209.90 as Ch30. Reconciliation compares two projections per currency, exactly: ledger settled cash against broker settlement-date cash, and ledger trade-date cash (settled + receivables - payables) against broker trade-date cash. For IBKR these are the SettledCash and TotalCashValue account values. Both payables and receivables are settlement_obligation rows.
verifier_note: Confirmed. Eq 9.1's min(C_b,C_l) masks this for availability, but not for reconciliation. ADR-0006 already adds a PAYABLE liability with buy settlement Dr PAYABLE / Cr CASH.

disposition.resolution: A buy credits PAYABLE on trade date (ADR-0006) and availability subtracts payables at once. Settlement moves PAYABLE to CASH only when broker settled cash agrees exactly, and reconciliation compares ledger CASH plus due settlements with broker settled cash, reporting unsettled differences separately.

title: Deposits, withdrawals, interest, account-level charges and external trades have no bucket assignment or authorization rule

locations.quote: Unknown external trades are assigned to an external-owner bucket until attributed; they still reduce available capital.
Widening limits, raising capital or changing a running strategy's parameters requires an explicit owner action with an audit record.
Production adds external flows, corporate actions, corrections and currencies with explicit conservation rules.

explanation: Ch30 promises 'explicit conservation rules' for external flows, but none are written. The book does not say whether a deposit the broker reports raises Unallocated, which would bypass the owner action Ch10 requires. When a manual withdrawal, a market-data charge, debit interest or an external manual buy reduces broker cash, the book says it 'reduces available capital' but not which bucket shrinks. If no bucket shrinks, the buckets add up to more than the real assets, and Protected or Session claims become unbacked. An external position in a stock a session also holds can be counted as session-owned sellable quantity.
proposed_resolution: (1) A detected deposit credits an Outside (unauthorized) owner. Only an authenticated owner 'authorize capital' command moves value from Outside to Unallocated, up to the ceiling K. (2) Withdrawals and account-level charges (interest, data and platform fees) debit Outside, then OperationalBuffer, then Unallocated, in that order. Any remainder is booked to an AccountShortfall exception claim that halts new entries. It never silently reduces Protected or Session owners. (3) External trades post to ExternalOwner with their own lots, and their cash comes from Outside by owner transfer. Sessions can never sell ExternalOwner lots. A negative ExternalOwner cash balance is a shortfall and halts. (4) Credit interest and income on external holdings go to Outside. Conservation per currency includes all of these flows.
verifier_note: Confirmed: there is no text anywhere in the book assigning these flows to buckets. ADR-0006 'External activity' already decides deposits to an 'outside' owner, withdrawals from outside first, and manual trades to 'external' funded from outside.

disposition.resolution: ADR-0006 'External activity'. Any unexplained broker cash change is a blocking CASH_MISMATCH. The owner attributes deposits, withdrawals, interest or charges to `outside` with record_external_cash_flow; a withdrawal larger than outside cash is refused and stays blocking. Only authorize_capital moves value from outside to unallocated. Manual trades are owned by `external` with their own lots and funded from `outside`, otherwise a blocking OVERCOMMITTED case.
disposition.residual: Interest and account charges have no dedicated posting yet (the INTEREST and OTHER_FEES codes are unused); they are recorded as external flows of `outside`.

title: The 'authorized-capital ceiling' could bound three different quantities, and each yields a different unallocated amount on the Ch10 example

locations.quote: Maintain a global authorized-capital ceiling, daily loss trigger, cumulative loss allowance, concurrency limit and reserved operational cash.
Account economic assets are now $305, of which $105 is protected, $100 allocated to B and $100 unallocated.
no program should interpret an unset cap as infinity
"live_authorized_capital_cents": null,

explanation: Take K = $300 and Ch30's $105.80 protected. If the ceiling bounds all system-claimed assets, protected included, the room after A completes is $194.20, and after B's $100 Unallocated is $94.20, not the book's $100. If it bounds only active allocations, the room after B is $200 while only $100 of free settled cash exists, so the only thing preventing over-allocation is the cash check, which is itself ambiguous (Eq 9.1). The book's example implicitly treats the ceiling as owner contributions, since total assets ($305) exceed it, but never says so. Paper mode has no authorized-capital value at all; only the live field exists, and it is null.
proposed_resolution: K bounds cumulative net owner-authorized contributions: the sum of authorize-capital commands minus de-authorizations and withdrawals of authorized funds. Realized profits and protected proceeds never count toward or against K. Unallocated is a journaled owner balance: authorizations credit it, seed allocations debit it, and approved releases credit it. Every allocation also passes the settled-cash check F. In live mode a null K means zero authority. In paper mode K is the simulated initial deposit and must be an explicit config value.
verifier_note: Arithmetic re-checked (300 - 105.80 = 194.20; 194.20 - 100 = 94.20). Severity lowered to medium, because the separate cash check bounds the dangerous direction when it is implemented correctly.

disposition.resolution: The ceiling bounds net owner-authorized capital: risk_state.authorized_total (authorizations minus deauthorizations) is capped by the policy's authorized_capital, which both shipped policies set explicitly (paper: 300.00). Protected proceeds and profits never count toward it, and every funding also needs unallocated settled cash.

title: The fee envelope's composition, size and release time are undefined, and the reference releases it on fill or cancel before fees are final

locations.quote: Before a buy, reserve limit price times remaining quantity plus a conservative fee envelope.
Remaining reservations are released only after terminal broker confirmation or conclusive reconciliation.
Terminal status does not mean every fee or correction has arrived.
Commissions can arrive after fills. Maintain estimated and final amounts separately.
order["fee_left"] = 0
"operational_fee_buffer_cents": null,

explanation: Ch9 line 27 releases reservations at terminal broker confirmation, and Ch13 line 7 says terminal status does not mean the fees have arrived. Whether the fee part of a reservation is released at order-terminal or at fee-final is therefore open. The reference zeroes fee_left on FILLED (line 254) and on confirmed cancel (line 272). IBKR delivers commissionReport separately from, and after, execDetails. A commission booked after release is taken from session cash that may already back other holds, which pushes session cash below its reservations. The envelope's contents are also unspecified: minimum per-order commission, per-share rate, caps, SEC/FINRA sale fees, India STT, stamp duty and GST, EU FTT, and FX fees. The deployment record also folds Ch9's fee buffer and Ch6's 'separate operational buffer' into one field.
proposed_resolution: Size the envelope per order as the sum over a versioned fee schedule: max(min commission, rate*qty), capped as the schedule specifies, plus exchange and regulatory fees, transaction taxes and any FX fee. Each part is in the currency it is charged in and rounded up to cash precision. Release the quantity part of the hold when the order is terminal. Release the fee part only when a final fee record exists for every execution of the order. If a fee is still missing after a configured interval, move the remainder into a session-level PendingFeeHold that end-of-day fee reconciliation clears. A final fee above the envelope posts in full, opens an exception and freezes the session. Configure fee_buffer and operational_buffer as separate values.
verifier_note: Confirmed; also checked engine.py:272, which zeroes fee_left on confirmed cancel too. Ch30's table admits the reference has only a 'fill-time envelope', but the book never states the production release rule. The overlap with the deployment-record buffer issue is intentional; that issue covers the config side.

disposition.resolution: The envelope is the policy fee model's uncapped per-share estimate (with its minimum) plus a margin, rounded up; the cash hold is ceil(leaves x limit x multiplier) plus the envelope not yet consumed by estimates. At order-terminal the unused envelope is released, but each execution's estimate stays accrued (FEES_ACCRUED, still subtracted from available cash) until the broker's commission replaces it. A final fee above the estimate is booked in full and its shortfall moves to a blocking OVERCOMMITTED case.
disposition.residual: The paper policy's fee schedule is marked UNVERIFIED, and regulatory fees and transaction taxes are not modelled (US sell-side fees accrue against the sale receivable). The single operational_buffer and the per-order envelope are separate values.

title: Multicurrency session accounting is undefined: session currency vs foreign holdings, valuing the target, FX P&L, and per-currency conservation

Apply the same reasoning per currency and account. A positive consolidated USD-equivalent balance cannot fund a EUR order unless actual permitted EUR cash or an explicit completed conversion exists.

title: No rounding mode for journal postings, fees or cost relief, and the book does not say whether the computed or the broker-reported amount is booked

explanation: Ch3 line 31 declares two rules: buy commitments round up, sellable quantity rounds down. No rounding mode (half-even, half-up or floor) is declared for journal postings, fee and tax computation, receivable estimates or cost relief. The unrounded p*q*M is stored as a memo, and any difference posts in the same transaction to a RoundingAdjustment line owned by the session. (2) Reservations and funding estimates are computed at full precision and rounded up per order; receivable estimates are rounded down. (3) Cost relief on a partial disposal is round-half-even(cost*q/Q), with the remainder kept in the lot, and the final disposal takes all remaining cost. (4) FX funding estimates use the adverse side, then round up. Add property tests for each rule.
verifier_note: Narrowed. The original said 'No chapter declares the rounding rule', but Ch3 line 31 declares two. disposition.resolution: Rounding is fixed by purpose (ADR-0004): reservations CEILING; execution notional HALF_EVEN at ledger scale with the raw notional kept; broker commissions booked as reported (HALF_EVEN to ledger scale); partial-disposal cost relief HALF_EVEN with the last disposal taking the lot's remaining cost; a settlement gap fully explained by recorded per-trade rounding is booked to ROUNDING.

title: The settlement state machine has no transitions, no rule for matching aggregate broker settled cash to individual obligations, and no outcome for an exception

locations.quote: The state machine is expected, pending, confirmed or exception. Only confirmation from an eligible account balance and reconciliation makes proceeds spendable under the conservative policy.
`COMPLETED_UNSETTLED`, `COMPLETED_SETTLED`

explanation: The book names four states but no transitions. Broker settled cash is an aggregate: several trades, fees and interest can settle on the same day, so 'confirmation from an eligible account balance' cannot by itself confirm one particular receivable. The book does not say when 'expected' becomes 'pending', or what causes 'exception' (a failed delivery, a partial settlement, a short-delivery auction). Nor does it say what an exception does to the Protected bucket or to the COMPLETED_UNSETTLED to COMPLETED_SETTLED transition.
proposed_resolution: Each settlement_obligation moves EXPECTED (booked, with its expected date computed under a recorded calendar version) -> PENDING (on or after the expected date) -> CONFIRMED, or to EXCEPTION. Confirm all obligations for one (account, currency, settle_date) together, and only when the projected ledger settled balance equals broker settled cash exactly; never pro-rate a partial match. Raise EXCEPTION if an obligation is not confirmed within N business days (configurable, default 2), if amounts differ, or if a correction arrives. Under EXCEPTION, funds stay non-spendable, new entries for that account halt, and the session stays COMPLETED_UNSETTLED. Close-out or auction differences post as adjustments to the owning bucket (Protected for completed sessions).
verifier_note: Confirmed: Ch9 line 43 is the only settlement-state text in the book.

disposition.resolution: Settlement rows move EXPECTED -> SETTLED, or to CANCELLED by a correction. All items due by the snapshot date are confirmed together, only when broker settled cash equals ledger CASH plus their net amount (or the gap is fully explained by recorded rounding); a partial match is never pro-rated, it is a blocking CASH_MISMATCH. An item still unconfirmed two business days after its expected date opens a non-blocking SETTLEMENT_LATE case and the session stays COMPLETED_UNSETTLED.

title: Corporate actions are not specified for session ownership, reservations, lots or completion

locations.quote: Corporate actions can alter quantities and basis without an ordinary trade.
| Inventory | Whole shares, average cost | Lots, actions and corrections |
Completion requires flat inventory, no unresolved orders, reconciled net proceeds and sufficiently finalized fees.

explanation: Stocks-first paper sessions that hold positions overnight will meet dividends and splits, and broker cash reconciliation will see them. The book does not say: whether a dividend belongs to the session and counts toward its target; how withholding is booked; what happens to a dividend whose pay date falls after the session went flat and completed; how a split adjusts open sell-quantity holds and buy-limit holds; how cash-in-lieu or untradeable fractional residue affects 'flat inventory'; or how mergers and delistings convert positions.
proposed_resolution: Book each corporate action as its own journal kind. A cash dividend is a receivable from ex-date, owned by whoever holds the lot on ex-date, with gross income and withholding as separate lines, settling on pay date. Completion may include pending dividend receivables at gross minus estimated withholding, rounded down; they become protected receivables and are trued up when paid. A split multiplies lot quantity by the ratio with basis unchanged. Open orders are re-reserved from the broker's adjusted order (qty*r rounded down, limit/r rounded up for buys), or stay fully reserved until the broker confirms a cancel. Cash-in-lieu is a disposal of the fractional lot. Mergers, delistings and untradeable residue move to ReviewHold and freeze the session.
verifier_note: Confirmed. The book defers corporate actions to 'production' (Ch30 line 61, Ch31 line 15) but does not mark them as a later track, and paper reconciliation will meet them.

disposition.resolution: Not implemented (LED-09 is `proposed`). A dividend, split, merger or delisting today surfaces only at reconciliation as a blocking POSITION_MISMATCH or CASH_MISMATCH, which keeps entries blocked; the owner can attribute cash only to `outside`, which would misattribute a session's dividend.
disposition.owner: I1 ledger extension (LED-09), needed before I2 paper sessions hold positions across an ex-date; data from I4 (DAT-03)

title: The cumulative loss allowance has no defined measure; the reference measures lifetime net P&L, so prior session profits silently enlarge the remaining loss allowance

locations.quote: no automatic replenishment of an exhausted loss budget
A human may replenish or revise a budget; an agent may not replenish its own loss allowance.
if state["realized_net"] + unrealized <= -state["loss_limit"]:

explanation: The book never says whether the cumulative allowance is lifetime net P&L, the sum of losing sessions' losses, or the peak-to-trough of non-protected equity. Each gives a different halt point. The reference uses lifetime realized_net, which includes completed sessions' already-protected profits. After A's +580 cents, the 200-cent limit fires only after 780 cents of further losses (580 + x <= -200). A probe on a temporary copy confirmed this: after A completed, a 100-cent mark-down on the successor reported net_marked_pnl = +480 and no halt. Under a net measure, the agent's own wins restore allowance it has already consumed, which Ch6 line 45 forbids.
proposed_resolution: Lifetime allowance consumed = the sum over terminated sessions of max(0, -session net P&L), plus the current marked loss of active sessions. Protected gains never offset it, and only an owner command raises it. The daily trigger is the net marked P&L of non-protected capital over the configured risk day, measured against K. Change the reference so completed sessions' P&L is excluded from the aggregate trigger, and add a test: profit in A, then a 200-cent loss in B halts.
verifier_note: Confirmed by running a probe on a temporary copy of the reference. Tightened the original wording that 'protected money funds the loss allowance': losses are paid from session or unallocated cash, and the defect is that protected gains offset the loss measure. In the reference, the 2% per-session drawdown (200 cents on a $100 seed) masks this for $100 sessions; it bites for larger seeds.

disposition.resolution: Cumulative loss = high-water mark of system P&L minus current system P&L, where system P&L is the marked value of every system owner (unallocated, buffer, session, protected) minus net authorized capital. Earlier gains, protected proceeds included, raise the high water and never refill the allowance; only a new policy widens it.

title: Outbox sender never says the attempt is persisted BEFORE transmission; a crash in that window resends a live order

locations.quote: The sender records attempt time and broker result. On restart, pending attempts are reconciled, not blindly replayed.
A crash after transmission but before acknowledgment produces an unknown result.
broker_order_id TEXT, last_attempt_at TEXT
`SUBMIT_PENDING`

explanation: 13:17 says the sender 'records attempt time and broker result' but not that the attempt is made durable before the bytes leave. If both are written after the broker call, a crash in between leaves a row that looks exactly like one never sent (attempt_count=0, last_attempt_at NULL). A restart that treats that row as unsent transmits it again, giving two live orders against one reservation. The phrase 'pending attempts are reconciled' implies a pre-send marker, but SUBMIT_PENDING is never defined as 'possibly transmitted' rather than 'queued', and the crash-recovery rule depends on exactly that distinction. The outbox holds one broker_order_id and one last_attempt_at per command, so a second attempt overwrites the identity that lookup needs to correlate the first. For IBKR the client assigns the orderId (and orderRef) before placeOrder. Recovery can correlate only if that id was stored before the send, and a placeOrder that carries the orderId of a working order modifies that order instead of creating a new one.
proposed_resolution: Use a write-ahead attempt protocol. Outbox states are READY -> SENDING -> {BROKER_ACKED, REJECTED, UNKNOWN}, and a separate outbox_attempt table holds (attempt_id, command_id, broker_correlation_id, broker_order_id, sent_at, result, raw_ref). Txn A, committed durably: re-check the stop latch, ownership epoch, transmit deadline and policy hash; allocate the broker correlation id (IBKR: orderId = max(nextValidId, stored high-water + 1), orderRef = command_id/attempt_id); insert the attempt row; set the outbox row to SENDING. Then transmit. Txn B records the result. On restart, every SENDING attempt without a result becomes UNKNOWN and goes to lookup. Only READY rows with zero attempts may be transmitted. An attempt's broker order id is never reused for a new order.
verifier_note: All four quotes verified. ADR-0009 (docs/adr/0009-order-lifecycle-and-outbox.md) already commits SUBMIT_PENDING before the broker call and recovers SUBMIT_PENDING by lookup, so the write-ahead decision exists outside the book. The book and the schema still lack per-attempt rows and a persisted broker correlation id. I softened the original IBKR id-reuse claim: TWS's nextValidId advances past ids it has received, so the real need is to persist the id/orderRef before the send so lookup can correlate.

disposition.resolution: Write-ahead (ADR-0009): outbox_begin commits SUBMIT_PENDING and the outbox row SENDING before the broker is called, and only PENDING rows are ever claimed, so a SENDING row is never sent again. On restart a SUBMIT_PENDING order or SENDING row becomes UNKNOWN with NEEDS_LOOKUP. The correlation id is the client order id in the order reference, and the IBKR adapter persists its orderId allocation before placeOrder and never reuses or resends it.

title: Reservation can be released on terminal broker status before the executions that status reports are ingested

locations.quote: Remaining reservations are released only after terminal broker confirmation or conclusive reconciliation.
Positions are derived from executions and corrections, not from an optimistic interpretation of order status.
An order status callback is not always the only evidence of an execution.
| Cancel/fill race | Apply fill, release only remainder | Correct quantity/cash |

explanation: Positions are derived from executions, but reservations are released on terminal status, and the book never says whose 'remaining' quantity governs the release: the broker-reported cumulative fill or the locally ingested executions. IBKR orderStatus carries filled/remaining, and execDetails can arrive later or only through a later query. If Cancelled(filled=6) arrives while 4 executions are ingested, releasing order_qty minus the ingested quantity frees cash for 2 shares that were bought. That cash can be spent before the late executions land, which overcommits the account. The worked example at 2:43 ('final remaining quantity is confirmed zero') and the fault-matrix row ('release only remainder') do not say which source defines the remainder.
proposed_resolution: Store broker_reported_cum_qty separately from ingested_exec_qty. On a terminal broker status, release only (order_qty - broker_reported_cum_qty) x limit plus the proportional fee share. Keep (broker_reported_cum_qty - ingested_exec_qty) x limit plus fees as an EXECUTIONS_PENDING hold. The order is economically closed only when ingested_exec_qty == broker_reported_cum_qty and every execution has a final commission. If the gap persists past a configured window, run executions_since with overlap. If the gap is still open after that, raise a reconciliation exception and block entries. Never reduce a hold on ingested quantity alone.

Reference probe (temp copy of reference/engine.py): when the cancel acknowledgment arrives before the final fill, `canceled` zeroes the hold based on local remaining and the late fill is then rejected. ADR-0009 releases `leaves_qty` without saying whether it is broker-reported or derived from ingested executions, so the gap remains open.

disposition.resolution: A terminal broker status whose filled quantity exceeds the ingested executions keeps the order's hold (broker_terminal_pending); the order turns terminal and releases only when ingested quantity reaches the broker's figure.
disposition.residual: A gap that persists is reported by reconciliation as a blocking EXECUTIONS_MISSING difference (recon.py:86-89); no test names that difference.

title: UNKNOWN has no exit rule: broker 'not found', retry identity and owner resolution are all unspecified

locations.quote: Order submission is different: after a timeout, query by durable identity before resubmitting. If the broker cannot reliably correlate a request, keep the result unknown and require reconciliation.
If the outcome remains unresolved, escalate to the owner and broker support through authorized channels.
async def lookup(self, command_id: str) -> SubmissionResult: ...
Reusing an identifier with a different payload is an error, not a retry.

explanation: The book says to query before resubmitting but never says which query result permits a resubmit or a reservation release. 'Not found' is ambiguous: the request may never have reached the broker, it may still be in flight (IBKR ApiPending/PendingSubmit), or the query may have covered only open orders. One engineer treats NOT_FOUND as rejected, then releases and resends, which duplicates the order if the original surfaces. Another keeps UNKNOWN forever, which traps capital and blocks green indefinitely because 13:23 requires clean reconciliation. lookup() returns SubmissionResult, whose documented statuses are ACCEPTED, REJECTED and UNKNOWN, so 'not found' cannot be expressed. The book does not say whether a retry keeps the command_id and gets a new broker correlation id. It also defines no owner action that closes an unresolved UNKNOWN.
proposed_resolution: lookup(order_key) returns a typed LookupResult: FOUND(status, cum_qty, broker ids), NOT_FOUND_CONCLUSIVE or NOT_FOUND_INCONCLUSIVE, with as_of and coverage. NOT_FOUND_CONCLUSIVE is allowed only when three conditions hold: the adapter's client-correlation capability is GUARANTEED; the query covered open orders, completed orders and executions for the attempt's trading day, each complete; and now >= attempt.sent_at + a configured correlation_settle_window (at least 2x the measured p99.9 acknowledgment latency). The attempt then becomes NOT_RECEIVED (terminal). The order service either releases the reservation or, if the transmit deadline, latch, policy hash and ownership epoch are all still valid, creates a new attempt under the same command_id with a new broker correlation id. Otherwise the order stays UNKNOWN, keeps its hold and blocks entries for the account. The owner resolves a stuck UNKNOWN through an audited resolve_unknown command that requires attached broker evidence (statement, confirm or support reference). That command can never release a hold while any broker source shows the order working.
verifier_note: Quotes verified. ADR-0009 permits a retry only after the broker 'conclusively reports that the order does not exist', and ADR-0012 gives lookup a found / not-found / unknown tri-state, but neither defines 'conclusive' or an owner resolution path. I softened one original claim: reusing an IBKR orderId the broker never received is technically allowed, but a new correlation id is still the safer rule.

disposition.resolution: lookup() is tri-state (found / conclusively not found / cannot determine). A conclusive 'not found' for an order with no fills makes it REJECTED and releases it; 'found' applies the broker status; 'cannot determine' keeps the order UNKNOWN, reserved and blocking. Nothing is resubmitted: a retry is a new intent with a new order id. The owner closes a stuck UNKNOWN with resolve_exception action close_unknown_order, which needs fresh authentication, a note and broker evidence (BROKER_STATEMENT, BROKER_CONFIRM or SUPPORT_REFERENCE) and never releases a hold the broker may still work: the latest reconciliation must be complete, in this process, fresh and later than the order's last material change (a repeated Inactive report counts), must not list the order as open or have found it by lookup, and may hold no other blocking difference; otherwise CLOSE_NOT_PROVEN names every unmet condition and nothing changes. The order ends REJECTED (no fills) or CANCELED (fills kept), its holds are released, UnknownOrderClosedByOwner records the evidence, run and lookup, and the account must reconcile again (RB-13).

disposition.residual: The IBKR adapter is conclusive only when placeOrder was never called, so a transmitted order with no trace always needs the owner's close. The evidence reference is recorded, not checked against a statement (statement ingestion, CAP-OMS-07, is not built). Neither the terminal nor the CLI offers the close: the owner sends it through POST /api/commands, and the terminal's acknowledge action resolves the case without closing the order (RB-13).

title: Red stop does not cover reserved-but-unsent outbox rows or SUBMIT_PENDING/UNKNOWN orders

locations.quote: The red button first persists a global stop latch and prevents new exposure-increasing commands. It then requests cancellation of open entries and records each outcome.
After approval, commit reservation and durable outbox in one transaction.
if order["side"] == "BUY" and self._open(order):

explanation: The outbox separates approval from transmission. If the latch is checked only when a command is evaluated ('prevents new ... commands'), rows already committed to the outbox are not 'new', so the sender can transmit them after the owner presses red, which adds exposure after a stop. 'Open entries' is undefined for SUBMIT_PENDING orders (possibly sent, broker id possibly unknown) and for UNKNOWN orders. An implementation that cancels only acknowledged or partially filled orders leaves those able to fill. The reference stop marks only OPEN/CANCEL_PENDING buys.
proposed_resolution: The sender re-reads every applicable stop latch (global, account, session) inside Txn A. If any is set, the row moves to WITHDRAWN (terminal, never sent) and its hold is released in the same transaction. On stop: (a) withdraw every READY exposure-increasing row; (b) send a cancel for every buy in SENDING/SUBMIT_PENDING, ACKNOWLEDGED/WORKING, broker-held, PARTIALLY_FILLED and UNKNOWN, using the persisted broker correlation id, plus a broker-level global cancel (IBKR reqGlobalCancel) when the account is dedicated to the platform; (c) track each cancel in the stop progress record until the order is broker-terminal. A risk-reducing sell row is exempt only when the active liquidation policy explicitly allows it.

ADR-0010 still enqueues cancels only for 'every open buy order', so SUBMIT_PENDING and UNKNOWN coverage remains undefined in both documents.

disposition.resolution: latch_stop cancels every open buy whatever its state: an untransmitted buy is canceled locally and its hold released; SUBMIT_PENDING, acknowledged, partially filled and UNKNOWN buys get an outbox CANCEL (by client order id, broker id optional) and keep their hold until the broker confirms. outbox_begin re-checks the entry gates inside its transaction, so a queued buy is never sent after a latch. Stop progress counts open buys, pending cancels and UNKNOWN orders. reqGlobalCancel is deliberately not used, because it would also cancel orders placed in TWS.

Tested through the gateway runner for price and quantity amendments, repeats, resolution and reconciliation. A correction of a completed session's execution posts to protected:<id> with an owner case (BR-LED-03).
disposition.residual: The reviewer's rule for a late lower or equal revision (store, do not apply) is not in the core: such a revision is not distinguished there. title: Broker read results carry no completeness, as-of time or scope, and nothing forbids inferring 'canceled' from absence

fetch a complete broker snapshot with its scope

explanation: The port returns untyped dicts and specifies none of the fields that 12:7 requires on every result. IBKR delivers open orders, executions, positions and account values as callback streams terminated by end markers (openOrderEnd, execDetailsEnd, positionEnd, accountDownloadEnd). A timeout before the marker yields a truncated list that looks valid. Compared against local state, it shows local working orders as missing at the broker. The book forbids marking everything canceled on a lost connection (8:31). It never forbids moving an order to a terminal state because it is absent from a list, so an implementer who maps 'missing' to CANCELED releases holds for orders that are still working and overcommits cash.
proposed_resolution: Every read returns a typed envelope: {items, complete, end_marker_seen, account_scope, request_id, broker_as_of, received_at_utc, received_at_monotonic, history_coverage_start}. Reconciliation aborts with no state changes, leaving entries blocked, if any required read is incomplete. A local working order absent from a complete open-orders list does not change state on that basis. Its absence triggers a lookup through completed orders and executions. Only an explicit broker terminal status, or owner-attested evidence, moves the order, and any release then follows the cumulative-quantity rule above.
verifier_note: Quotes verified. ADR-0012 already notes that the book's port is untyped and adds a completeness flag. Neither the book nor the ADRs forbid inferring a terminal state from absence, and ADR-0009's 'conclusive reconciliation' remains undefined.

disposition.resolution: Every port read is typed and carries a completeness flag. A reconciliation with any incomplete read (snapshot, open orders, executions, or a non-converging execution re-read) is INCOMPLETE and only keeps entries blocked. A local order absent from a complete open-order list is looked up; only a conclusive 'never received' for an order with no fills makes it REJECTED, and an acknowledged order missing at the broker is a blocking difference, never inferred canceled.
disposition.residual: The ORDER_MISSING_AT_BROKER and ORDER_UNRESOLVED branches (recon.py:98-101, 122-123) have no test of their own.

title: Order state is one enum in one column although the same chapter forbids collapsing state into one status string; no transition table

locations.quote: An order has intent, transmission and economic state. These must not be collapsed into one status string.
Use local states `CREATED`, `RESERVED`, `SUBMIT_PENDING`, `ACKNOWLEDGED`, `PARTIALLY_FILLED`, `CANCEL_PENDING`, `FILLED`, `CANCELED`, `REJECTED`, `EXPIRED` and `UNKNOWN`.
deadline_utc_ns INTEGER NOT NULL, state TEXT NOT NULL
return order["status"] in ("OPEN", "CANCEL_PENDING")

explanation: The enum mixes intent states (CREATED, RESERVED), transmission states (SUBMIT_PENDING, CANCEL_PENDING, UNKNOWN) and economic states (PARTIALLY_FILLED, FILLED), and the schema stores them in a single `state` column, which is the collapse 13:3 forbids. 13:7 stores quantities independently, so 'cancel pending with fills' is representable. What is missing is a transition table and several states. CANCEL_PENDING overwrites ACKNOWLEDGED or PARTIALLY_FILLED, so a cancel rejected as too late has no recorded state to return to. There is no state for broker-held or inactive orders (IBKR PreSubmitted, Inactive). The book does not say whether executions are accepted in CANCELED, FILLED, REJECTED or SUBMIT_PENDING. Without a table, each engineer decides which transitions are legal and which ones release holds. The reference uses another vocabulary again (OPEN).
proposed_resolution: Use three orthogonal fields plus quantities. intent_state: {CREATED, APPROVED_RESERVED, WITHDRAWN, EXPIRED_UNSENT, REJECTED_LOCAL}. transmission_state: {NOT_SENT, SENDING, WORKING, HELD, CANCEL_PENDING, REPLACE_PENDING, UNKNOWN, BROKER_TERMINAL}. broker_terminal_reason: {FILLED, CANCELED, REJECTED, EXPIRED, NOT_RECEIVED}. Quantities: broker_cum_qty, ingested_exec_qty, open_qty. Executions are accepted in every transmission_state. Publish the transition table as code, with an IBKR mapping: ApiPending/PendingSubmit -> SENDING, PreSubmitted -> HELD, Submitted -> WORKING, PendingCancel -> CANCEL_PENDING, ApiCancelled/Cancelled -> CANCELED, Filled -> FILLED, Inactive -> HELD until a reject reason makes it REJECTED. A cancel reject returns the order to its prior working state and keeps the stop progress item open. The single UI status is a derived projection only.
verifier_note: Quotes verified. I tightened the explanation: the original said the enum 'cannot represent' cancel-pending-with-fills and UNKNOWN-with-fills, which overstates the gap because 13:7 stores quantities independently. The confirmed defect is the single mixed column, the missing transition table and the missing held/inactive states. ADR-0009 adds a separate cancel_state but keeps the mixed enum.

disposition.resolution: One published order transition table: core/order_machine.py declares every state change with its reason, and Context.emit checks every order row a handler writes against it before anything is recorded, so no handler can take an order anywhere the table does not list. An undeclared change is refused and recorded instead as an OrderTransitionRefused event (keeping the received broker payload), a blocking critical ORDER_TRANSITION_REFUSED case and the stop latch; a terminal state is never left. Quantities, fees, cancel_state and prev_state stay beside the state label (ADR-0009), executions are accepted in every state, and a cancel rejected as too late restores the prior state. Decision on held orders (ADR-0009 amendment): IBKR PreSubmitted is ACKNOWLEDGED (working); Inactive becomes UNKNOWN with every hold kept, a blocking unknown-order case and, for a buy, a cancel; only a broker terminal report or the owner's close on evidence releases it (it used to be released as REJECTED). A locally terminal order that a reconciliation finds Inactive is a blocking anomaly, and a buy is canceled.
disposition.residual: ADR-0009 keeps one state label rather than the reviewer's three orthogonal fields; a broker-held order is UNKNOWN plus a broker_held record, not a separate HELD state. The real IBKR sequences that produce Inactive have not been observed (no paper session; docs/integrations/ibkr.md section 5, item 4).

title: Amend/replace reservation rules cover only buy increases; there is no in-flight state and no execution attribution after a modify

locations.quote: Store replacement chains for amendments. Increasing a buy's limit or quantity requires a new risk check and extra reservation before the change is sent. A cancel-and-replace can temporarily leave both orders exposed if the broker does not provide atomic replacement semantics.
an amendment rejected after the old order filled
command_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES order_intent(command_id),

explanation: The book leaves five amendment cases undefined. (a) A decrease in quantity or limit: releasing the difference at send time is unsafe, because the old terms can still fill until the broker confirms the change. (b) A non-atomic cancel-and-replace: the hold must cover the old remaining quantity plus the new order, and the book does not say so. (c) An IBKR in-place modify (placeOrder with the same orderId): the hold must be max(old, new) until the change is confirmed. (d) Execution attribution after a modify: one broker order then serves several commands, but outbox and order_intent are keyed on command_id and execution.command_id is a single FK. (e) The amendment has no in-flight state. A sell-side quantity increase, which must reserve more inventory, is also missing. 13:41 nevertheless requires 'an amendment rejected after the old order filled' as acceptance evidence.
proposed_resolution: Either (preferred for the foundation) exclude amendments from the first eligibility profile and remove the 13:41 amendment item from foundation acceptance, or adopt these rules. An amendment is a new command (amend_command_id, parent_command_id, broker_order_key) with its own payload hash and risk check, and transmission_state is REPLACE_PENDING while it is in flight. In-place modify: hold max(old_open_qty x old_limit, new_open_qty x new_limit) plus fees until the broker confirms, then shrink to the new terms; on reject, keep the old terms. Cancel-replace: hold the old open quantity plus the full new order until the old order is broker-terminal, then release the old remainder under the cumulative-quantity rule. A decrease releases nothing until confirmed. Executions attach to broker_order_key and are attributed to the version in force at the broker's execution time (fallback: the latest confirmed version). A sell quantity increase must reserve additional unreserved inventory before it is sent.
verifier_note: Quotes verified. ADR-0009 already bans cancel/replace in the initial eligibility ('no cancel/replace'), which conflicts with the book's 13:41 acceptance item. The resolution now names that choice explicitly.

disposition.resolution: ADR-0009 'Initial order eligibility' excludes cancel/replace and in-place amendment: a replacement is a broker-confirmed cancel followed by a new intent with a fresh risk check. No amend command exists and BrokerCapabilities.atomic_replace defaults to false, so the book's 13:41 amendment acceptance item is outside the initial profile.

explanation: _open() is true only for OPEN and CANCEL_PENDING. An execution delivered after the cancel confirmation, the race that 2:25 and 13:3 call normal, is therefore rejected and rolled back. I tightened 'reservation stays held forever' to 'until a local cancel command is issued'.

disposition.resolution: The core ingests executions in every order state: a fill after CANCELED or FILLED is booked with a blocking EXECUTION_ANOMALY, never discarded; unsolicited broker CANCELED and EXPIRED statuses apply without a local cancel request; delivery order does not change the result. title: BrokerPort lacks the methods and result fields the book requires (auth state, stream, completed orders, commissions, amend, account scope, global cancel)

title: OrderIntent and the order_intent table disagree with each other and with the command contract (missing TIF, session eligibility, account; scales dropped)

quantity_units INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(quantity_units > 0),

title: Intent deadline is undefined: last transmit time vs working-order expiry; EXPIRED is overloaded

deadline_utc_ns: int

explanation: The deadline could mean (a) the last time the intent may be transmitted, (b) the time by which a working order must be canceled, or (c) a GTD value sent to the broker. The book's single EXPIRED state could mean either a local deadline miss or broker TIF expiry. Under (a) alone, an order sent 1 ms before its deadline rests for the whole DAY and can fill hours after its signal has died. It is also unclear whether a retry after an UNKNOWN resolves is bound by the original deadline. The deadline is compared against a wall clock that can step, so an expired intent can look fresh.

A transmitted order lives until the broker's DAY expiry, which arrives as a broker EXPIRED status with its own reason. Nothing is retried automatically.

title: Reconciliation tolerances have no values: 'material', 'clean' and 'approved tolerances' gate trading but are never defined

locations.quote: Snapshot pagination and concurrent fills require a consistent cut or an explicit convergence loop.
disables additional exposure when the difference is material or unexplained.
Resume only after a fresh reconciliation meets the approved tolerances.

explanation: Positions, cash and open orders are fetched by separate requests at different instants while fills continue and local ingestion lags. A fill that lands between the positions read and the executions read produces a phantom quantity difference. The book allows either a consistent cut or a convergence loop, but gives no termination rule and no outcome for non-convergence. 'Material' (8:27), 'clean reconciliation' (13:23) and 'approved tolerances' (26:23) have no values, and config/paper_defaults.json has no tolerance fields. These terms decide whether trading is blocked. One implementation freezes on every busy reconciliation; another adds a cash tolerance that hides a small missing fill. 9:49 forbids only a 'broad' monetary tolerance.
proposed_resolution: Use a convergence loop. (1) E1 = executions_since(watermark - overlap), complete. (2) S = positions, balances and open_orders, each complete, with broker_as_of recorded. (3) E2 = executions_since(same cursor). Ingest E1 and E2. If E2 holds executions not in E1, or any open order's cum_qty changed, repeat, up to 5 times with backoff. If the loop does not converge, report NOT_CONVERGED, which keeps entries blocked but is not a mismatch. Comparison is per (account, instrument). Quantity tolerance is exactly zero in the quantity scale. Cash tolerance is at most 1 minor unit per execution in the window, and any nonzero cash difference is booked as an explicit ROUNDING adjustment with a reason. Differences in the order or execution sets are never covered by a tolerance. Classify results as MISSING_LOCAL_EXECUTION, MISSING_BROKER_ORDER, EXTERNAL_TRADE, EXTERNAL_ORDER, FEE_DIFF, VALUATION_ONLY or CORPORATE_ACTION_SUSPECT. Tolerance values live in the versioned policy.
verifier_note: Quotes verified. I retitled the issue: the book explicitly allowing either a cut or a loop is not unsafe by itself. The confirmed defect is that the thresholds that gate trading have no values in the book, config/paper_defaults.json or the ADRs.

disposition.resolution: Clean means no blocking difference. Quantity tolerance is zero per instrument; cash must agree exactly except a gap fully explained by recorded per-trade rounding (booked to ROUNDING); order and execution set differences are never tolerated. The reconciler re-reads executions after the snapshot for up to three rounds; non-convergence or any incomplete read is INCOMPLETE (entries blocked, not a mismatch).
disposition.residual: The values are fixed in code rather than the versioned policy; the non-convergence branch and the order-set difference kinds have no test of their own.

title: Execution watermark has no type or advance rule, and nothing covers a broker history window shorter than the outage

explanation: The book does not define the watermark (broker cursor, execution time or receipt time), the overlap size, or what happens when the broker cannot serve history back to the watermark. IBKR's API execution query covers a limited recent window, the current day by default (TWS can extend it to a few days). After a weekend outage, a multi-day authentication lapse or a restore from backup (24:21), executions_since cannot reach the watermark, and an implementation that treats the returned set as complete silently loses fills. 12:41 names 'missing execution history' as a test case but specifies no behavior. Advancing the watermark to the maximum execution time can also skip late-reported executions that carry earlier timestamps.
proposed_resolution: The watermark is the adapter's broker cursor when one exists. Otherwise it is receipt-ordered, with overlap >= a configured max_report_delay (default at least one full trading day). executions_since returns history_coverage_start. If coverage_start > watermark - overlap, the result is HISTORY_GAP: entries for the account are blocked, a statement-based backfill (for IBKR, a Flex/activity-statement import) or an owner-attested acceptance is required, and the gap is recorded in the reconciliation report. The watermark advances to min(max ingested receipt time, broker_as_of - overlap), and only after the report commits.
verifier_note: Quotes verified. ADR-0012 adds an 'execution-history depth' capability but defines no behavior when the depth is shorter than the gap.

disposition.resolution: The watermark is the adapter's cursor, stored on the reconciliation run and reused only from the last CLEAN run; overlap is de-duplicated on exec keys. The IBKR adapter reports executions incomplete when its history cannot reach back across a gap, and entries stay blocked until the owner records acknowledge_history_gap, which needs fresh authentication and forces a new reconciliation.
disposition.residual: Statement (Flex) backfill is not implemented; the owner attestation is the only way past a gap.

(b) For an external sell of an instrument a session holds, the book does not say whether it reduces EXTERNAL or session inventory. Applying it to the session gives the session P&L from a trade it did not make. Applying it to EXTERNAL drives external inventory negative while the session still believes it owns the shares and may sell them, creating a short in a cash account. (c) The book does not treat orders or executions that carry this platform's tag format with an unknown command_id as split-brain evidence.
proposed_resolution: Reconciliation creates an EXTERNAL_ORDER record for each unmatched broker open order. It reserves the full notional plus a fee envelope (buys) or the quantity (sells) against the EXTERNAL owner and blocks entries in that instrument until the order is terminal or the owner attributes it. External executions post to EXTERNAL inventory and cash. If EXTERNAL quantity would go negative, the deficit becomes a SESSION_INVENTORY_DEFICIT exception against the session(s) holding the instrument: their sellable quantity drops immediately and their entries freeze until the owner attributes the trade. Unmatched items with this platform's orderRef prefix or clientId trigger the split-brain path (red latch).
verifier_note: Quotes verified, and the grep found no book text on external working orders. ADR-0011 latches on foreign-tagged or untagged activity, which covers (c) and partly (a). ADR-0006 routes manual trades to the `external` owner but does not handle an external sell of shares a session holds.

disposition.resolution: Resolved. (a) and (c): any broker open order or execution not matched to this deployment's orders (another tag, no tag, or an unknown id) is FOREIGN_ACTIVITY, blocking, and latches the stop. (b): a manual sale relieves `outside`, then `external` lots, never session lots; if a session holds the instrument and the sale cannot be covered, a critical blocking EXECUTION_ANOMALY ('manual sale may have used session-held shares') is opened, and a blocking EXECUTION_ANOMALY refuses further reducing sells (pretrade BLOCKS_REDUCTION), so the session cannot sell the same shares again until the owner resolves it.
disposition.residual: test_f30_manual_sale_of_session_shares_is_flagged_not_netted_silently asserts the blocking case, not the refused follow-up sell; the refusal comes from the open EXECUTION_ANOMALY, which test_f36 shows blocks a reducing sell.

title: Risk reduction is allowed during reconciliation failure, but 'confirmed' inventory is then undefined

explanation: When reconciliation has failed, inventory is by definition not confirmed, and the book does not say which quantity bounds a reduction sell. Using the local ledger quantity oversells when the broker holds fewer shares (after an external sale or a missed correction), which creates a short in a cash account. Using the broker quantity can sell shares that belong to the external owner or to another session. 'Appropriately controlled' is undefined.
proposed_resolution: While reconciliation is not clean: sellable(session, instrument) = floor_to_increment(min(local session qty - that session's held sell qty, fresh complete broker qty - all held sell qty across owners - EXTERNAL claims)). If broker positions are stale or incomplete, sellable = 0. Reduction orders must be limit orders inside the collar, require an enabled liquidation policy and are journaled as REDUCTION.
verifier_note: Both quotes verified, and the two sentences do conflict as written. ADR-0010 defaults on_stop_liquidation to NONE but does not define sellable quantity during a reconciliation failure.

disposition.resolution: Resolved. Sellable quantity is the session's own unreserved lots; a sell needs a clean reconciliation in this process. POSITION_MISMATCH, FOREIGN_ACTIVITY, EXECUTION_ANOMALY and LEDGER_INVARIANT cases block reductions (OPEN_EXCEPTIONS), while a cash-only difference does not. Both sides are now tested: a cash difference permits a reducing sell, and an open EXECUTION_ANOMALY refuses one.
disposition.residual: The refusing test uses EXECUTION_ANOMALY; no test opens a POSITION_MISMATCH and then attempts a sell. The test asserts the refusal, not its code (OPEN_EXCEPTIONS was confirmed by re-running the scenario on 2026-10-22).

title: Clearing authority for the different blocks and latches (unknown order, auth, reconciliation, restart) is undefined
