The service must enter an authentication-required state, notify the owner and resume only after reconciliation.
It clears the latch only after the checks pass. An automatic process restart cannot clear it.
A restart begins in reconciliation-required mode.
Blockers identify concrete causes such as unresolved position difference, expired broker authentication, unset live capital or unavailable market data.

explanation: The book defines several blocks: the owner red stop, the account unknown-order 'latch', reconciliation failure, authentication required, restart reconciliation-required, session RISK_STOP and queue overflow. It does not say who may clear each one. 12:17 reads as an automatic resume after re-authentication and reconciliation, while 22:26 lists expired authentication as a green-preflight blocker, which implies the owner must press green. The unknown-order 'latch' in 26:19 could be taken for the red latch, which only green clears. One engineer auto-resumes trading after IBKR's daily re-authentication; another makes the owner press green every day.
proposed_resolution: Represent blockers as durable rows: {kind, scope (global/account/session/instrument), raised_by, reason, raised_at, clear_policy}. OWNER_STOP is cleared only by an authenticated owner green action after full preflight. RISK_STOP requires owner review followed by green. System blocks (UNKNOWN_ORDER, RECON_FAILED, AUTH_REQUIRED, HISTORY_GAP, QUEUE_OVERFLOW, STALE_DATA, RESTART_RECON_REQUIRED) are cleared only by the writer, and only when their specific recovery evidence is recorded, such as the id of a converged clean reconciliation report. A restart never clears a blocker, and process start always inserts RESTART_RECON_REQUIRED. Entries are permitted only when no blocker applies in scope.
verifier_note: Quotes verified. I added the 22:26 quote, which sharpens the 12:17 tension. ADR-0010 covers the restart recovery gate (auto-resume off by default) and makes reconciliation failure a latch that needs green. AUTH_REQUIRED and UNKNOWN_ORDER clearing are still unmapped.

disposition.resolution: ADR-0010 and the runbook conventions. The stop latch (owner red, loss budget, reconciliation failure, foreign activity, restore, invariant failure) clears only through an owner green start with preflight. Conditions clear on evidence: an UNKNOWN_ORDER case resolves on broker evidence; a disconnect or lost authentication sets needs_reconciliation, cleared by the next clean reconciliation; a process restart sets the recovery hold, cleared by an owner start or, only when the policy allows and no latch is set, by a clean reconciliation.

title: Retained fee buffer has no size, duration or release trigger

locations.quote: Commissions can arrive after fills. Maintain estimated and final amounts separately.
Terminal status does not mean every fee or correction has arrived.
order["fee_left"] = 0

explanation: 9:33 says 'Retain a fee buffer before making funds reusable' but not how much, until when or from which bucket. The reference releases the remaining fee envelope as soon as an order is FILLED (line 254) or CANCELED (line 272). If a production port does the same and a commission report (IBKR sends one per execution, separately and sometimes later) or a regulatory fee exceeds the fill-time estimate, session cash falls below its holds or below zero.
proposed_resolution: Store fee_estimate and a nullable fee_final per execution. After an order is terminal, its fee hold = sum over executions with fee_final null of (fee_estimate x a configured safety factor), plus any order-level minimum-commission exposure. Each part is released when that execution's final commission arrives. An execution still lacking a commission after a configured window (for example, the T+1 statement) is reconciled from the statement. A session cannot complete while any fee hold remains.
verifier_note: Quotes verified (also engine.py:272). I changed the kind from contradiction to omission: chapter 30's reference-to-production map already labels the reference's fees 'Fill-time envelope', with 'Delayed finalization and adjustments' as the required extension, so the reference does not contradict the book. The confirmed defect is that the book never sizes or times the retained buffer.

disposition.resolution: Each execution's estimated fee stays accrued (FEES_ACCRUED, or against the sale receivable) until the broker's commission replaces it; a session cannot complete while any execution is neither FINAL nor an owner-accepted estimate; an overrun posts in full and opens a blocking OVERCOMMITTED case.

title: On disconnect, 'mark affected orders unknown' conflates an uncertain submit with a stale view of a working order

locations.quote: On lost internet, block new entries and mark affected order outcomes unknown.
A lost broker connection should set order state to unknown where appropriate; it must not mark everything canceled.

explanation: 'Affected' and 'where appropriate' are undefined. If a disconnect moves every working order to UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN comes to mean both 'did my submit reach the broker' and 'my view of a known working order is stale'. The UNKNOWN recovery path (lookup, then possible retry) could then resubmit orders that were acknowledged long ago. IBKR orders keep working on the server while the API client is disconnected.
proposed_resolution: A disconnect never changes the transmission_state of an acknowledged order. It sets account-level status_stale_since and raises a CONNECTION/AUTH blocker. Only commands with an attempt in SENDING (submit, cancel or amend) at the moment of disconnect become UNKNOWN. On reconnect, a full converged reconciliation refreshes every order before the blocker clears.
verifier_note: Quotes verified. ADR-0009 makes a disconnect during submit UNKNOWN but says nothing about already-acknowledged orders.

disposition.resolution: A disconnect only records connectivity and sets needs_reconciliation; acknowledged orders keep their state. Only a submission or cancel in flight at the failure becomes UNKNOWN, and on restart only SUBMIT_PENDING or SENDING rows do. Entries resume after a clean reconciliation has refreshed every order.
disposition.residual: No test asserts that an ACKNOWLEDGED order keeps its state across a disconnect; broker_connectivity (broker.py:791-803) only updates the control row.

title: 'Fail closed' on lossless queue overflow is undefined for inbound broker events

locations.quote: If a lossless queue exceeds its capacity, fail closed and preserve diagnostic state.
Quotes can sometimes be replaced by newer snapshots; fills and money events cannot.

explanation: For inbound execution, order-status and commission callbacks, 'fail closed' could mean dropping the event, rejecting it at enqueue or crashing. Each of these removes the event from the live path, because the socket callback has nowhere else to go and IBKR does not redeliver callbacks. Recovery then depends on a later re-query, which works only within the broker's execution-history window. The book also does not say whether order-status events may be coalesced.
proposed_resolution: Every inbound broker event is first appended to a durable raw-event journal, before processing, so the in-memory queue can be bounded without loss. If the journal append fails or lags beyond a bound: raise QUEUE_OVERFLOW, disconnect the API session, and after reconnect recover through a full reconciliation using executions_since with overlap. Order-status events may be coalesced per order only to the latest non-terminal status. Terminal statuses, executions and commissions are never coalesced.
verifier_note: Quotes verified. I tightened the original 'all three lose fills': dropped executions can be re-queried, but only inside the broker's history window, which makes the gap real but conditional.

disposition.resolution: Every inbound broker event is appended to a durable, hash-chained, append-only journal (<account>.events: fsync'd, with the core store's durability settings) before it is applied. Each entry is applied under its own deterministic command id and then marked, so a crash between append and apply loses nothing, and a crash between apply and mark re-applies it as a stored-result duplicate. At start the service applies unapplied entries before any request or new event. The in-memory hand-off is bounded: if the journal cannot be written, the runner stops taking events (at most one batch waits in memory), latches the stop (EVENT_JOURNAL_UNWRITABLE), records an INCOMPLETE reconciliation and, in pump(), fails closed before the outbox pass, so no new buy is transmitted; journaled entries are still applied. A corrupt or conflicting entry is never applied; the verified entries before it are. Events are never dropped or coalesced (identical IBKR status messages are de-duplicated). Tested for crashes at every point, SQLITE_FULL, corruption, restored cores and a seeded randomized scenario with ledger invariants and replay checks (ADR-0012 amendment; RB-15).
disposition.residual: An event the adapter has received but the gateway has not yet appended (in the adapter's own in-memory FIFO, or in the gateway's single batch) is lost at a crash and recovered only by reconciliation, inside IBKR's execution-history window (a gap needs owner acknowledgement). While the journal fails, the adapter's FIFO keeps growing in memory and the API session is not disconnected. The journal is not in the online backup and is never pruned.

title: Three versions of the optimistic check (expected policy version, expected state version, policy hash) with no scope for automated intents

locations.quote: Commands include a deadline and expected policy version.
A command includes authenticated identity, immutable command ID, expected state version, policy hash, deadline and typed intent.
policy_hash: str
Starting after a stop requires owner authentication and a fresh state version.

explanation: 8:19 asks for an expected policy version, 30:7 for an expected state version plus a policy hash, 8:15 for both a policy version and a state version, and OrderIntent carries only policy_hash. The scope of 'state version' is undefined. If it is the global ledger version (the reference increments it on every command), every fill invalidates in-flight strategy intents and causes constant rejections. If it is ignored, an order sized on a UI screen from an old balance passes. The book also does not say whether the version is part of the hashed payload, which decides how idempotent retries behave.
proposed_resolution: Orders carry policy_hash, which must equal the session's snapshot hash, and expected_allocation_version, scoped to the (session, account) allocation record. That version changes only on allocation actions by the owner or coordinator, not on fills or holds. Risk is always re-evaluated inside the writer transaction against current state, and a mismatch in either field gives REJECTED_LOCAL with reason STALE_CONTEXT. Both fields are part of the payload hash, and an identical retry returns the original recorded decision. Control commands (green) use the account control-state version.
verifier_note: Quotes verified, and the reference does increment state['version'] on every command (engine.py:88). I added 22:26 and 8:15 as further variants.

disposition.resolution: Intents carry policy_hash, which must equal the session mandate's (POLICY_VERSION check). Risk is re-evaluated against current state inside the writer transaction, so no global state version is needed, and the payload hash covers policy_hash, so an identical retry returns the stored decision. Green start runs preflight and clears the latch in the same transaction.

title: Parent/child schedule reservation: the book does not say whether a child's reservation transfers from the parent or adds to it

locations.quote: It must reserve the full economic commitment, not only the current child order, unless the allocator explicitly controls the remainder.

explanation: If the child's reservation is added on top of the parent's, cash is double-reserved and funding stalls. If a terminal child releases its unfilled amount to free cash instead of back to the parent, the parent's remainder is under-reserved and another strategy can claim that cash. The price at which the parent reserves, and whether a repriced child may exceed the parent's price bound, are also unspecified.
proposed_resolution: The parent holds a PARENT reservation = parent_open_qty x parent_price_bound + fee envelope. Creating a child atomically transfers child_qty x child_limit (child_limit <= parent bound) from the parent reservation to the child. A terminal child returns its unfilled part to the parent, not to free cash. The parent's remainder is released only when the parent is terminal, all its children are broker-terminal, and the cumulative-quantity rule is satisfied. A child limit above the parent bound is rejected locally. Until this is implemented, parent schedules stay out of the eligibility profile.
verifier_note: Quote verified, and the ambiguity is real. This is not on the 14-day critical path: ADR-0009's initial eligibility allows only plain DAY limit orders. The book does not mark schedules as a later track, so the issue stays at medium with a 'keep out of eligibility until implemented' rule.

disposition.resolution: No parent/child schedule exists, so neither reading of the book can occur.
disposition.limitation: No parent/child schedules: every intent is a single DAY limit order with its own hold; there is no parent reservation and no child transfer. Schedules stay outside the eligibility profile until a parent-reservation design is adopted.
disposition.documented_in: docs/adr/0009 'Initial order eligibility' (limit orders only, no cancel/replace) and this file

title: Split-brain fencing cannot be enforced at IBKR, and the book does not say where the token is checked

locations.quote: A fencing token checked by the execution gateway provides stronger protection than a lease alone. If a broker cannot enforce fencing, route all account commands through a single credential-owning gateway and require explicit failover reconciliation.
Prefer a single credential-owning gateway with fencing or require manual transfer of execution ownership after reconciliation.
| Split brain | One fenced writer | Rejected stale leader |
Establish connectivity, obtain valid order identifiers, subscribe to account/order state, reconcile, then enable entry submission.

explanation: IBKR's TWS API checks no client-supplied token. Any process that can reach a logged-in TWS or IB Gateway with a free clientId can place orders, and orderId sequences are per API client. The fault-matrix row expects a 'rejected stale leader', but no IBKR component will reject one. 24:27 leaves the design as 'Prefer ... or ...': one engineer builds automatic database-lease failover, which 24:27 itself says can fail during a partition, and another builds manual transfer. The ledger writer and the broker adapter are separate processes in 8:9, and no rule says the sender re-checks the writer's epoch inside its send transaction. A stale gateway can therefore transmit outbox rows that a new writer considers unsent. Two hosts on the same paper username also contend, because IBKR allows one session per username.
proposed_resolution: Foundation decisions: (1) Broker credentials for a given account live on exactly one host. IB Gateway binds to localhost, the API trusted-IP list is 127.0.0.1, and one fixed clientId is allowed for order entry. The Mac uses a distinct paper username. (2) A monotonically increasing ownership epoch row in the ledger DB. Every send transaction (Txn A) and every ledger mutation compares the epoch inside the same transaction and aborts on mismatch. (3) No automatic failover. Ownership transfer is an owner command that increments the epoch, requires evidence that the old host is stopped or its broker session terminated, and requires a full converged reconciliation before green. (4) An order or execution whose orderRef/clientId was not issued under the current epoch is split-brain evidence and automatically sets the red latch. Change the 28:30 fault-matrix evidence to 'stale host cannot transmit (local epoch check) and foreign-tagged activity latches the stop'.
verifier_note: Quotes verified, and I added 28:30. I lowered severity from critical to high: the book does state the safe fallback (8:37) and defers automatic multi-region failover (8:39). The residual defects are the open 'prefer ... or' choice and a fault-matrix expectation IBKR cannot meet. I dropped the original 'Mac logs in with the live username' scenario because 24:3 already restricts the Mac to paper credentials. ADR-0011 adopts manual transfer, order tagging and a fixed clientId.

disposition.resolution: ADR-0011: the fence is local. Every write transaction checks the writer-lease epoch, so a superseded process cannot claim or send an outbox row; transmission also needs this deployment's HELD execution ownership; every order carries deployment:epoch:client-id; foreign-tagged or untagged activity latches the stop; ownership moves only by owner command with a release certificate or an attestation. The IBKR adapter uses a fixed client id and latches on 'client id in use' or an unexpected account.

title: Availability formula 9.1 has no session-allocation term, an undefined R, and a P that includes receivables, so it misstates fundable cash

locations.quote: Define broker-eligible settled cash $C_b$, ledger settled cash $C_l$, reconciled restrictions $H$, already committed cash $R$, protected proceeds $P$ and operational buffer $B$. A conservative availability bound is
These terms must be disjoint.
Separately track policy buckets: unallocated capital, session allocations, protected proceeds, order reservations and operational buffers.
Once completion is reconciled, lock the session's economic value in a protected policy bucket. Unsettled proceeds remain receivables.
It funds the successor from independently available, unallocated, eligible cash.
The session retains $9.90 cash plus $95.90 receivable, totaling $105.80. Completion protects both components.

explanation: 9.1 is the book's only quantitative definition of 'available'. It subtracts H, R, P and B from settled cash. Line 7 names five policy buckets, but 9.1 has no explicit session-allocation term, and R ('already committed cash') is never defined: it may or may not include session allocations. Ch.10:17 and Ch.30:15 put unsettled receivables inside protected proceeds, so P is not disjoint from settled cash, which breaks the disjointness that line 19 requires. Recomputing the Ch.30 example after A completes and B is funded: settled cash = 300 − 90 − 0.10 = $209.90; P = $105.80 ($9.90 settled + $95.90 receivable); true unallocated = $100. If R excludes allocations, 9.1 = 209.90 − 105.80 = $104.10, overstating by $4.10. If R includes B's $100, 9.1 = $4.10, understating by $95.90. Neither reading gives $100. Also, 9.1 is not bounded by the authorized-capital ceiling (Ch.10:35). That ceiling exists, but nothing ties it to this formula, so an account holding more than the authorized amount yields a larger A.
proposed_resolution: Make `unallocated` a ledger bucket, not a residual of broker cash. Only owner-signed capital authorizations and defined internal returns (closed-session residuals, an enabled seed recycle) credit it, and a successor is funded only from this bucket. Rewrite 9.1 as an account- and currency-level consistency check that runs before every funding commit: min(C_b, C_l) − H ≥ Σ session settled cash (including reservations) + P_settled + B + unallocated. Receivables never count. If the check fails, block funding and open a reconciliation exception. Cap unallocated so that Σ allocations + unallocated + protected ≤ authorized capital. Add the Ch.30 numbers as a test (expected available = 10,000 cents).

Narrowed one claim: the authorized-capital ceiling does exist (Ch.10:35); the defect is that 9.1 does not reference it. ADR-0006 line 59 has already re-interpreted 9.1 as 'minus every non-outside claim', which agrees with this resolution.

title: No rule for an execution, bust or correction that arrives after a session is COMPLETED: session state, inventory owner and paying bucket are all unspecified

locations.quote: A completed session has no position or open order.
In production, real broker anomalies must be ingested through exception accounting rather than discarded to preserve an artificial nonnegative invariant.
if session["state"] == "COMPLETED" and (session["positions"] or session["cash"]):
a canceled order may still have earlier fills arriving late.
Execution busts and corrections require reversal entries plus replacement events.

explanation: The book requires such events to be ingested (Ch.28:9 and CLAUDE.md:21), so a production port does not have to reject them. What it never says is what the event does to the session. A late fill on a canceled order, a bust of a sell fill, or a price correction can arrive for a session that is already COMPLETED, with its proceeds protected and its successor funded. Open questions: does the session re-open; does its success status or its successor change; who owns the resulting inventory; which bucket pays the cash difference (protected, the successor, or unallocated); does the account latch? Two implementations would end with different owners for both the money and the shares.
proposed_resolution: Completed sessions are never re-opened and never leave COMPLETED_*. Any execution, bust or correction linked to a completed session's order is journaled to an `exception:<case>` owner attributed to that session. Inventory is held there. Cash effects post against the session's protected bucket, and any shortfall becomes an exception claim against unallocated. Every such event sets an owner latch on the account. Residual inventory is reduced only under the Ch.13:25 narrow-reduction rule. The session gets a `post_completion_adjusted` flag; its success status and its successor are unchanged. Restate the Ch.28 invariant as 'no position or open order outside the exception owner'.

Ch.28:7 is scoped to 'the simplified reference', and Ch.28:9 explicitly mandates exception accounting in production, so the book does not tell implementers to reject the fill. The gap is session and bucket handling, which is real. ADR-0008 covers late fees and corrections against protected:<id> but not late fills that create inventory.

disposition.resolution: A completed session never re-opens and never leaves COMPLETED_* (ADR-0008 amendment). Any later execution, bust, correction or fee for its orders is booked to whoever holds its balances now (protected:<id>; unallocated after CLOSED); its outcome and successor do not change, and one blocking POST_COMPLETION_ADJUSTMENT per execution names that owner. A fill on a terminal order also opens an EXECUTION_ANOMALY, and a shortfall moves to exception:<case>. Inventory that lands there is reduced only by an owner DISPOSAL sell of that owner's lots through the full pretrade. Tested: a late fill after completion and after close, a bust of the wind-down sell, a bust of a buy whose shares were already sold, a bust while the order works, and a price correction after COMPLETED_SETTLED, each with the ledger invariants and replay checked.

title: Unsuccessful sessions have no terminal path, no rule for residual capital and no successor rule

locations.quote: A session can terminate unsuccessfully, wait indefinitely for an admissible opportunity or be stopped by the owner.
A successful transition has a single successor request keyed by the completed session identifier.
Repeatedly restarting losing sessions can consume the whole authorized account even if each session has a small stop.

explanation: The book never says what makes a session terminate unsuccessfully, which state it ends in (STOPPED or FAILED_REVIEW), where its remaining equity goes (unallocated, protected or held), or whether anything follows it automatically. A grep of docs/book finds no residual-capital rule. One engineer returns the residual to unallocated and lets the coordinator start a replacement, which is exactly the account-draining loop Ch.6:45 warns about. Another strands the residual inside a dead session. A third question is also open: if a session closes above seed but below target, is that profit protected like a successful session's, or recycled?
proposed_resolution: Unsuccessful terminal conditions are: session risk trigger, loss budget exhausted, owner end, eligibility or artifact revocation, optional max duration, and target observed but not realized. Path: → WINDING_DOWN(reason) → RECONCILING → STOPPED (terminal, flat). STOPPED never creates a successor request. Once the session is flat with no open or UNKNOWN orders and fees are final, return settled residual up to the seed to unallocated and send any amount above the seed to protected; receivables follow the same split when they settle. A new session after a STOPPED one needs an explicit owner command and must pass the cumulative-loss-allowance check.
verifier_note: Confirmed: docs/book has no residual-capital or unsuccessful-terminal rule. Note that accepted ADR-0008 (docs/adr) already decided differently on two points. It splits STOPPED into SUSPENDED and CLOSED. On CLOSED it moves ALL cash and receivables to unallocated, with no seed/profit split. The orchestrator should reconcile the proposed above-seed→protected split against ADR-0008.

disposition.resolution: ADR-0008: an unsuccessful session winds down, reconciles and ends CLOSED with an outcome (BELOW_TARGET, OWNER_ENDED, EXPIRED); all its cash and receivables return to `unallocated` (receivables stay non-available until settled); no successor is created; loss budgets are account-level and survive sessions, restarts and policy versions.
disposition.residual: ADR-0008 returns everything to unallocated; the reviewer's split (amount above seed to protected) was not adopted. The RISK_ENDED outcome has no trigger yet: session risk triggers suspend instead.

title: Cumulative and daily loss budgets are not defined as gross or net, and the reference nets lifetime profits, so protected gains refill the loss allowance

locations.quote: A human may replenish or revise a budget; an agent may not replenish its own loss allowance.

if state["realized_net"] + unrealized <= -state["loss_limit"]:
"cumulative_loss_allowance_cents": null,

explanation: 'Consumed loss allowance' is never defined, in particular whether gains offset losses. The reference measures lifetime realized_net, which includes profits already moved to protected. Probe (temp copy): after one completed session (buy 10 at 1000, sell at 1060, no fees), realized_net = 600. The aggregate trigger then fires only when the successor's unrealized loss reaches −800 cents, against a 200-cent limit. The agent's own wins have refilled the allowance with money that is no longer at risk. A gross or per-session measure behaves differently. The book also never says whether a session may be funded when the remaining allowance is smaller than that session's loss budget.
proposed_resolution: Cumulative consumption = Σ over terminated sessions max(0, seed − final net value) + Σ over active sessions max(0, seed − current liquidation value) + unattributed losses (exception-ledger losses, unattributed fees). Profits of completed sessions never reduce consumption. Only an owner-signed BUDGET_REVISION policy version raises the allowance. A session may go to READY only when remaining allowance ≥ its loss budget; otherwise it stays WAITING_FUNDS with reason LOSS_ALLOWANCE. An exhausted allowance sets an owner latch.

In that probe the 2% session drawdown trigger fired first (at a 200-cent loss), so the inflation is in the aggregate allowance specifically. That matters across sessions and when drawdown is not the binding trigger.

disposition.resolution: Same resolution as BR-LED-20: cumulative loss is measured from the high-water mark of system P&L, so protected gains never refill the allowance; the daily trigger is measured from the first valuation of the risk day.
disposition.residual: Funding does not compare the remaining allowance with a new session's loss budget; a breach blocks every entry.

title: The 10-state session machine has no transitions, triggers, guards or terminal states, and the reference uses different states

title: Whether an ordinary (non-emergency) tightening reaches running sessions is contradictory, and the owner may apparently widen a 'immutable' running session

proposed_resolution: Latches are per broker account, plus an installation-wide latch that sets every account latch. Store them in the fenced writer's ledger and mirror them in an fsync'd file at the credential-owning gateway. The gateway checks (fencing token, latch epoch) on every exposure-increasing submit. The Chapter 26 latch covers UNKNOWN only, and it sits in an ops runbook, not in the strategy contract.

For buys, count it as fully filling when testing exposure increases. For sells, count it as reserved when computing sellable inventory. Use the same definition in the pretrade concentration and aggregate checks. A15 emits no new intent for an instrument with any UNKNOWN or CANCEL_PENDING order. A pending buy counts as if it fills and a pending sell as already sold; terminal orders count nothing. The core's CONCENTRATION check adds the session's open buys in the instrument and GROSS_EXPOSURE every open buy of the account, each tested by a rejection against a control. The runner uses the same definition, emits no new intent for an instrument with an UNKNOWN or CANCEL_PENDING order in the session (PENDING_UNRESOLVED), allows at most one live intent per session, artifact and instrument (OPEN_INTENT), and checks both at the decision and again at transmission. title: Eq. 6.4 sizing leaves fixed and minimum fees out of the risk term; the worked example permits a trade whose loss at the stop is 3.5x its budget

If cash allowed 2 shares, the loss would be $2.00 (4x), which equals the whole 2% session drawdown trigger (paper_defaults: 200 bps of a $100 seed). The text only says the commission 'might' make the strategy unsuitable, when the sizer should output zero. The cash term also subtracts only the fixed allowance f, not per-share variable fees, so it can disagree with the Chapter 9 reservation (limit × quantity + fee envelope). Both fees come from risk.fees.envelope, the function the core reserves fees with (minimum per order included), under the active policy's fee model at runtime and the engine's schedule in the backtest; zero means no order. title: No rule for assigning availability time to backfilled or date-only historical data

locations.quote: The feature's availability time is the earliest time the system could actually use it. A filing published at 14:00 but received at 14:03 cannot influence a simulated 14:01 decision.
