explanation: The no-merge, no-deploy rule covers only research-generated code. Claude Code writes all the production code. The book requires no branch protection, no owner review, no signing-key custody outside agent reach, and no deploy path that accepts only owner-signed artifacts. A coding agent holding push and deploy credentials could change hard-coded risk checks, bypassing signed policy, and ship them. R13's 'unauthorized mutation tests' would not catch this.
proposed_resolution: 1) Protect main: merges need approval from the owner's account with hardware-key 2FA, and agent tokens can push only to feature branches. 2) Only the owner holds the release-signing key (hardware key or Secure Enclave), on no path agents can read. 3) Before activation, the execution host verifies the signature and the approved-registry entry. 4) Changes to risk, ledger or authority code paths are marked authority-sensitive and need explicit owner sign-off. 5) Claude Code sessions hold no deploy credentials.

disposition.resolution: Not resolved. The owner's instruction of 2026-10-22 lets agents fast-forward main after CI is green; nothing in the repository enforces owner review or signed releases.
disposition.missing: Branch protection with owner approval, an owner-held release-signing key, a deploy path that verifies the signature, and owner sign-off for authority-sensitive paths.

title: There is no model-egress data policy: licensed-data rights are one global boolean, provider fallback can leak licensed content, and account data can reach third-party models

locations.quote: Data agreements may distinguish display, non-display, derived data, storage, redistribution and AI processing.
"model_processing_rights_verified": false,
Provider diversity can improve resilience
An operator assistant explains state and suggests owner actions.
Cloud-provider processing rights must be checked for licensed news, transcripts and estimates.

explanation: Processing rights depend on the dataset, the provider and the retention mode, but the deployment record holds one global boolean. verifier_note: Quotes verified. Partly addressed: Ch 23 l.31 says to keep entitlement evidence 'per deployment and provider', and Ch 17 l.39 puts deletion obligations in the source registry. The book specifies neither a fallback rights re-check nor classification of account data. Outside foundation scope; severity lowered to medium.

Agent code cannot import ledger or execution modules, and every input artifact or tool result must belong to a registry dataset that grants cloud processing, so balances and account ids have no path into a context.

title: Alerting has no channel, acknowledgment, escalation timer or dead-man's switch, and no defined behaviour when the owner is unreachable

locations.quote: Rate-limit duplicate alerts and attach a runbook. The owner remains the escalation endpoint when a provider requires human authentication or a policy decision.

explanation: The book defines alert severities but not how an alert reaches the owner. A host that dies, or a Mac that sleeps, cannot raise its own alert, and no external heartbeat is specified.
proposed_resolution: Alerts go through at least two independent channels (push plus SMS or email) via a provider off the execution host. Immediate alerts repeat every 5 minutes until the authenticated owner acknowledges them; acknowledgment does not clear the underlying condition. The execution host sends a heartbeat to an external monitor, which alarms after 2 missed intervals. While an immediate alert is unacknowledged, the account stays entries-blocked. verifier_note: Quotes verified; every listed element is absent from the book. This is operations scope (the day 13-14 drills), not the ledger foundation; severity lowered to medium.

disposition.resolution: Not implemented: there is no alert channel, acknowledgement, repeat or external heartbeat. The core latches the stop after 3, 10 and 100 consecutive cycle failures and exposes adapter anomalies through a broker_alerts query.
disposition.missing: Two independent off-host alert channels, owner acknowledgement with repeat, and an external dead-man heartbeat.

title: CLAUDE.md's reading list and 'next milestone' order conflict with the reading guide and the Ch 27 build sequence

title: The pretrade sequence has no self-cross/wash-trade check, although Ch 25 requires preventing self-crossing

explanation: Reproduced on a scratch copy: BUY B 10@900 with fee budget 10; cancel then canceled sets the reservation to 0; BUY B2 11@900 immediately reserves the freed 9,900; a late execution E9 on B (10@900, fee 10) is then refused with Rejected('invalid simulated fill or exceeded fee envelope'). If _open is patched to admit CANCELED orders, check() raises AssertionError('reservation exceeds cash') and the fill is rolled back anyway. Chapter 9 line 29 and Chapter 31 line 13 already say the simulator's rejection is synthetic-only and that production must ingest such fills through an exception journal, so the discard itself is a documented reference limit. The book-level gap that remains is the release rule: Ch.9 line 27 releases the remainder on terminal confirmation alone, while Ch.13 line 3 and Ch.12 line 13 say executions can arrive after that confirmation. No rule ties the release to the broker's reported cumulative filled quantity. Followed as written, the cash is handed to another order and the late fill can only land as an overdraft exception.
proposed_resolution: A terminal cancel/expiry/reject confirmation releases only (order qty minus broker-reported cum_filled_qty) times limit, plus the unused fee envelope. It releases even that only when cum_filled_qty equals the sum of ingested executions for the order. Any shortfall stays reserved as 'awaiting executions' until the missing executions are ingested or reconciliation proves them absent. Execution ingestion never checks order status, fee envelope or reservation sufficiency. It journals the fact, deduplicated by scoped execution id. If the fact overdraws the session, post it, open an exception record, charge the deficit to the operational buffer and then unallocated, and set the global new-exposure halt. 'Cash >= reservations' is an acceptance rule for commands, not an invariant enforced on ingestion.

The book explicitly marks fill rejection as simulator-only (Ch.9 l.29, Ch.31 l.13: 'Unexpected real broker events require exception ingestion rather than the simulator's synthetic-input rejection'), so 'built as written, the platform loses track' overstates the case. The release-timing omission is real: Ch.28 l.23 says 'release only remainder' but never defines remainder against broker cum-filled.

disposition.resolution: Release follows the broker's cumulative quantity (BR-ORD-02): a terminal status ahead of its executions keeps the hold; a fill after a terminal state is booked with a blocking anomaly, never rejected; a shortfall moves to exception:<case> and blocks new exposure.

explanation: _cmd_stop changes only local status. It creates no cancel command id and no outbox row; in a simulator this is expected, but the contracts that production is meant to build on cannot do better.
